findings.summary: Specification: the test's data is said to have no subnormal operand (so A = (|A| @ |B|)[i, j]); float16 torch.randn data does have subnormal operands.
findings.detail: README, Specification, the paragraph after the tolerance table: "On the test's data (no subnormal operand, so A = (|A| @ |B|)[i, j]), the claim bounds the test's error measure by 1.6e-5 to 1.03e-3 per shape". A standard normal value lies below 2^-14 (the smallest normal float16) in magnitude with probability 4.87e-5, so a float16 torch.randn matrix of the test's sizes is expected to hold about 13 to 1600 subnormal values; a CPU run of torch.randn(dtype=torch.float16) after torch.manual_seed(0) at the test's shapes gave 3 to 102 per matrix (the device's generator differs, the distribution is the same). With a subnormal operand, A = dotMag exceeds the normaliser by (max(|a_k|, 2^-14) * max(|b_k|, 2^-14) - |a_k * b_k|) for each such k: at most 1.9e-7 relative on the sampled shapes where it was computed. So the per-shape figures stand to the digits given; only the parenthetical is wrong. Resolve: say that A is the normaliser up to that excess, negligible on such data, so the bounds hold to the digits given.
findings.evidence: work/subnormals.py and work/subnormals.out: subnormal operands per matrix (a, b) 0/0 at 512^3, 3/4 at 1000^3, 8/10 at 3072x4096x1024, 6/0 at 257x129x4097, 0/0 at 64^3, 102/93 at 8192x8192x4096; max A/(|A|@|B|) - 1 = 1.90e-07 at 1000^3 and 4.85e-08 at 257x129x4097.

notes: No blocking finding. The model was printed with full names (work/print_model.out): every operation is TVA.*, Assumptions is a structure with exactly (K, P), and main uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Every test launch meets Inst.ok, and the README's tolerance table was recomputed in exact arithmetic (work/check_conditions.py, work/check_conditions.out).
